$comment: Dev evaluation labels for midday (scripts/eval.py). findings: the Phase 2 corpus review of a sample of findings, copied from corpora/labels/midday.json (reviewed entries only). knownPositives: a source-only audit by an AI agent (Claude) that read only the project's source at the pinned revision and did not run Midwrite or see its output (2026-11-06). Midday is the dev set: rules may be tuned against it. No independent human review has been performed.

knownPositives.scope: unhandled half-written-state windows in server code; the audit was capped at 30 entries, highest confidence first, so the list is a sample when the project has more

knownPositives.consequence: If the enqueue fails the job retries, but the invoice is already 'unpaid' so the retry exits at the status!=='scheduled' guard (line 34). The scheduled invoice is never generated or emailed, yet shows as sent/unpaid.

knownPositives.firstEffect: notifications.create('invoice_sent', sendEmail) emails the customer at line 91
knownPositives.secondEffect: updateInvoice status='unpaid', sentTo, sentAt at line 135
knownPositives.consequence: If the DB update throws after the email went out, BullMQ retries (attempts:3) and the customer gets the invoice email again. If it returns null, the invoice stays draft/unsent though the customer has it.

knownPositives.firstEffect: markInvoiceGenerated for an existing draft/scheduled invoice at line 208
knownPositives.consequence: If the enqueue fails, the series counter has already moved on. The next run looks for sequence+1, so the existing draft/scheduled invoice for this period is never sent, and the recurring schedule treats it as generated.

knownPositives.firstEffect: transactions upsert (ignoreDuplicates, returns only new rows) at line 50
knownPositives.consequence: If a trigger fails, the task throws and retries. On retry the upsert returns no ids (the rows already exist), so enrichment and inbox matching are never triggered. The bank transactions stay uncategorized and unmatched to receipts.

Imported rows are committed. If an enqueue fails, the retry's onConflictDoNothing returns no ids, so allTransactionIds is empty and enrichment/matching are skipped for good. If only the first trigger succeeds, transactions are enriched but never matched.

knownPositives.firstEffect: provider.syncTransactions creates transactions in Xero/QuickBooks/Fortnox at line 267
knownPositives.secondEffect: upsertAccountingSyncRecord per result at line 281 (catch at 425 marks whole batch 'failed')
knownPositives.consequence: If a sync-record write fails after the provider accepted the batch, nothing records the provider transaction ids, and the catch block marks the whole batch failed. The next export pushes them again, creating duplicate bookkeeping entries in the accounting system.

knownPositives.firstEffect: attachments uploaded to the provider via throttledConcurrent/uploadSingleAttachment (provider.uploadAttachment) starting at line 198
knownPositives.consequence: If the mapping update fails or the worker dies after the uploads, the mapping does not list them. The retry (attempts:4) uploads them again, leaving duplicate receipts attached to the transaction in Xero/QuickBooks.

If the trigger fails, the connection row (and its access token) is already gone from Midday but the connection is never revoked at Plaid/GoCardless/Teller/EnableBanking. Bank consent stays active (and billable) with no record left to retry from.
If the enqueue fails, the invoice shows as unpaid/sent but no PDF is generated and no email reaches the customer. The user gets an error for an invoice that already left draft.

knownPositives.firstEffect: draftInvoice at line 449 / updateInvoice status='unpaid' at line 487
knownPositives.secondEffect: triggerJob('generate-invoice') at line 499 (scheduled path: triggerJob('schedule-invoice') at 529)
knownPositives.consequence: If the enqueue fails, the API client gets a 500 but the invoice already exists (unpaid with no PDF, or a draft). The client's retry creates a duplicate invoice with a new invoice number.

knownPositives.secondEffect: bank_accounts insert (no conflict handling, separate statement) at line 176
knownPositives.consequence: If the accounts insert fails, a connection row with fresh tokens exists but has no (or stale) accounts. The UI shows a connected bank with no accounts, and the initial sync has nothing to sync.

knownPositives.firstEffect: transaction_attachments insert per inbox item at line 1317
knownPositives.secondEffect: inbox update to status 'done' with attachmentId at line 1374 (transactions tax update at 1359 in between)
knownPositives.consequence: If a later write fails, the transaction already has the receipt attached (and maybe tax copied), but the inbox item still shows unmatched. Retrying the match inserts the attachment again, leaving duplicate attachments.

knownPositives.secondEffect: supabaseAdmin.auth.admin.deleteUser at line 79 and resend.contacts.remove at line 80 (all in Promise.all)
knownPositives.consequence: These run concurrently with no compensation. If the Supabase auth delete fails, the user row and teams are gone but the auth account still exists, so the person can sign in to an empty account. If it succeeds and the DB delete fails, data remains for an account that can no longer sign in. The marketing contact may be left either way.

knownPositives.firstEffect: mark all unnotified transactions notified=true at line 24
knownPositives.consequence: If the notification or email fails, the error is caught and logged (line 61) and the task succeeds. The transactions are permanently flagged notified, so the team never gets the new-transactions email or activity.

knownPositives.dbAccess: deleteUser -> db.delete(users) and db.delete(teams) in Promise.all
knownPositives.secondEffect: db.delete(teams) for single-member teams at line 146
knownPositives.consequence: These are concurrent, independent commits. If the team delete fails, the user is gone but their solo team (bank connections, transactions, invoices) is orphaned with no members, and a retry cannot find it.

knownPositives.secondEffect: transaction_attachments delete by path at line 336
knownPositives.consequence: If the second delete fails, transactions still show attachments for a file the document list no longer has (and the router then removes it from storage). A retry returns NOT_FOUND because the document row is gone.

knownPositives.firstEffect: triggerJob('delete-team') (revokes bank connections at providers) at line 180
knownPositives.consequence: If deleteTeam fails or the request dies after the enqueue, the cleanup job still revokes every bank connection at the providers. The team survives with bank connections that look connected in the DB but are dead.
If the trigger fails, the invites exist (and show as pending) but no email is sent. Re-inviting the same addresses is skipped by onConflictDoNothing and validateInvites, so the emails never go out.

knownPositives.firstEffect: triggerJob('schedule-invoice') at line 484 then removal of the previous scheduled job at line 513
knownPositives.secondEffect: updateInvoice with the new scheduledJobId at line 537
knownPositives.consequence: When rescheduling, the old job is removed before the DB update. If updateInvoice then throws, the invoice still points at the removed job, and the new job is skipped as stale (id mismatch). The invoice stays 'scheduled' and is never sent.

knownPositives.firstEffect: BullMQ job.remove() of the scheduled send at line 760
knownPositives.secondEffect: updateInvoice status draft, scheduledJobId null at line 765
knownPositives.consequence: If the update fails after the job is removed, the invoice shows 'scheduled' with a date but nothing will ever send it.
If the update fails, the reminder email goes out but reminderSentAt is not recorded. The UI offers the reminder again, and the user's retry emails the customer a second time.

If the DB write fails, Polar has reactivated the subscription but the team keeps canceledAt set. A retry finds no canceled subscription (NOT_FOUND), and no handled webhook clears it, so the team stays flagged canceled (cancellation follow-ups, isTeamStillCanceled).

If the trigger fails, the connection and accounts exist but no daily sync schedule is created and no initial sync runs. The bank shows as connected with no transactions, and the user only sees an error.

knownPositives.secondEffect: Supabase storage remove from 'vault' at line 83
knownPositives.consequence: If the storage remove fails, the DB rows are gone but the file stays in the vault bucket with no record. It is orphaned and keeps sensitive financial data the user asked to delete, and a retry returns NOT_FOUND.

knownPositives.firstEffect: enrichment status set to 'pending' at line 145
knownPositives.consequence: If the enqueue fails, the customer is stuck showing 'enriching/pending' forever. Unlike upsert (lines 97-107), no compensating reset is done.
If an enqueue fails, the user gets an error though the transaction was saved. It is never enriched or matched, and the user's retry creates a duplicate manual transaction.

knownPositives.dbAccess: GenerateInvoiceProcessor.process -> updateInvoice(db) filePath, then two queue adds
knownPositives.consequence: If the second enqueue fails, the job retries (attempts:3) and enqueues send-invoice-email again, so the customer receives the invoice email twice or three times.

RedisCache.delete swallows errors and skips when disconnected. If invalidation fails, the deleted key stays cached and keeps authenticating REST calls through the auth middleware for up to the 30-minute TTL.

knownPositives.function: anonymous openapi handler (GET gmail oauth callback)
knownPositives.firstEffect: inbox account with OAuth tokens saved at line 126
knownPositives.consequence: If the trigger fails, the user is redirected to an error page, but the Gmail account is stored with no sync schedule and no initial sync. It shows as connected and never imports attachments.

knownPositives.dbAccess: checkInvoiceStatus.run -> supabase insert transaction_attachments, then updateInvoiceStatus (supabase update invoices)
knownPositives.firstEffect: transaction_attachments insert linking the invoice PDF at line 60
knownPositives.consequence: If the status update fails (supabase errors are not thrown), the invoice PDF is attached to the matching transaction but the invoice stays unpaid/overdue. The transaction is now fulfilled, so later runs never match it again.

The two writes go to disjoint transaction rows (updates vs noUpdateNeeded), and each row update sets enrichmentCompleted on its own, so no invariant spans them. On a thrown error the catch at enrich-transaction.ts:202-217 marks the whole batch completed on purpose (comment 209-210). On a crash, BullMQ retries (transactions.config.ts:14, attempts: 3), and getTransactionsForEnrichment (transaction-enrichment.ts:58) re-selects only rows with enrichmentCompleted=false, so the retry converges and the leftover partial state is harmless. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 returned-builder change.)

invoice-payments.ts:528-550: PaymentIntent is created with a deterministic idempotencyKey (invoice id+amount+currency); if updateInvoice fails the client gets a 500 and a retry sees no paymentIntentId and gets the same intent back from Stripe, then saves it. An unconfirmed intent charges nothing, so the window converges by design. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

rest/routers/invoices.ts:556-575: job.remove() runs only when updateInvoice returned no row, so the update matched nothing and committed no change. The remove is the compensation for the triggerJob at 528. The claimed commit-then-effect state does not exist. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

billing.ts:294-306: if updateTeamById fails after Polar cancelAtPeriodEnd, the Polar subscription.canceled webhook (webhooks/polar/index.ts:148-166) also sets teams.canceledAt, so the DB converges without the request. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

billing.ts:339-349: Polar is uncanceled first, then canceledAt is cleared. If the DB write fails, a retry hits NOT_FOUND (the sub no longer has cancelAtPeriodEnd, line 330) and the Polar webhook handler has no uncanceled/updated case to clear canceledAt. teams.canceledAt stays set (read by isTeamStillCanceled, teams.ts:715). (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

trpc/invoice-payments.ts:149-161: refund then status update; comment at 154-155 relies on the Stripe charge.refunded webhook (webhooks/stripe/index.ts:169-201), which sets status=refunded/refundedAt if the inline update is lost. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

invoice-recurring.ts:509-563: DB changes commit in one transaction, and job removal is deliberately done after commit (comment 557). A leftover schedule-invoice job is harmless because ScheduleInvoiceProcessor skips invoices whose status is not 'scheduled' (schedule-invoice.ts:35-42). (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

invoice-recurring.ts:580-633: same pattern as delete. Invoices are reverted to draft in one transaction and jobs are removed afterwards on purpose. A stale job no-ops because schedule-invoice.ts:35 checks status !== 'scheduled'. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

trpc/invoice.ts:505-543: the old scheduled job is removed before updateInvoice records the new scheduledJobId. If the update fails or the process crashes in between, the DB still points at the removed old job, and the new job is skipped as stale by schedule-invoice.ts:60-72. The invoice stays 'scheduled' and is never sent. updateSchedule (lines 725-732) avoids this by removing only after the DB update. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

trpc/invoice.ts:484-519: the new job is created first on purpose (comment 483, 503). If removing the old job fails or is interrupted, the comment at 514-515 accepts it: the DB still points to the old job, and the orphan new job no-ops in schedule-invoice.ts (status/stale-id checks). (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

trpc/invoice.ts:545-553: job.remove() is on the !data path, where updateInvoice matched no row and committed nothing. The remove is cleanup of the orphan job, so there is no DB commit before it. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

trpc/invoice.ts:699-710: newJob.remove() runs only when updateInvoice returned no row (no committed change). It is the compensation for the triggerJob at 677, so the claimed commit-then-effect window is not real. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

trpc/invoice.ts:692-732: the DB is updated to the new job id first, then the old job is removed best-effort with .catch. The comment at 728-729 says a leftover old job is detected as stale by the processor (schedule-invoice.ts:60-72). (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

trpc/invoice.ts:760-773: the BullMQ job is removed before the invoice is reset to draft. If updateInvoice fails, the invoice stays 'scheduled' with scheduledJobId pointing at a deleted job: the UI shows a scheduled send that will never happen. Only a manual retry fixes it, and the reverse order would be safe given the processor's status guard. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

user.ts:77-85 with users.ts:139-145: the DB delete of the user and sole-member teams and supabaseAdmin.auth.admin.deleteUser run concurrently in Promise.all with no compensation. If the DB delete succeeds and the auth delete fails, the user's data is gone but the auth account can still sign in. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

user.ts:79-83: the auth user delete and resend.contacts.remove run concurrently, and the Resend SDK reports errors in its return value rather than throwing. If the contact removal fails after the account is deleted, the email stays in the marketing audience, and a retry is impossible once the auth user is gone. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

process-document.ts:147-157,184: the path goes through `!uploadedData` (upload returned no data, i.e. failed) into the catch-block fallback update at 184, so no upload was durably performed before that DB write. On the success path the upload is an in-place upsert that a BullMQ retry redoes. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

process-document.ts:44-63: the document_uploaded notification is wrapped in try/catch as non-critical. If the job stops before the HEIC upload, BullMQ retry (attempts 3) reruns the conversion; at worst the activity notification is duplicated. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

process-document.ts:147-160,317: the converted JPEG overwrites the same vault path (upsert). If the job stops before classify-image, BullMQ retries (documents queue attempts 3); sharp re-converts the already-JPEG file (image-processing.ts:145) and classification is triggered, so the job converges. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

process-document.ts:147-166 vs 305: the HEIC upload path always sets processedMimetype='image/jpeg', which then takes the image/ branch and returns at 330. classify-document at 472 is only reached on the non-image else path, so the upload and this effect are mutually exclusive. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

inbox/process-attachment.ts:108-139: in-place upsert of the converted JPEG, then contentType is updated. A BullMQ retry (inbox attempts 3) reloads the item, re-converts and updates again; the job is idempotent and converges. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

slack-upload.ts:148-176: upload is an upsert to a deterministic path and createInbox uses ON CONFLICT on referenceId slack_<fileId> (inbox.ts:1786). A BullMQ retry (default attempts 3) converges. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

sync-scheduler.ts:198-239: uploadedAttachments contains exactly the uploads that returned data, so the reported `uploadedAttachments.length > 0` else path means no upload succeeded and no durable effect precedes updateInboxAccount. Even on the success path, lastAccessed is not advanced until the end, so the next sync re-uploads (upsert) and converges. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

sync-scheduler.ts:207,247-249: uploads are upserts to deterministic paths and lastAccessed is updated only at 283. If the job stops before process-attachment is enqueued, the retry or next sync re-fetches (no inbox rows exist yet), re-uploads and enqueues; process-attachment dedupes via getInboxByFilePath/ON CONFLICT. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

sync-scheduler.ts:251-271: the inbox_new notification is in try/catch, explicitly non-critical ('Don't fail the entire process'). The reported path (length>0 yet map body not run) is contradictory, but the upload-then-notification window is real and accepted. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

generate-invoice.ts:60-90: the PDF goes to a deterministic path (invoiceNumber.pdf) with upsert, and a DB update failure throws, so the job retries (job-client default attempts 3) and overwrites idempotently. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

export.ts:214-235: the code labels the documents-table update 'non-critical' (line 227). If it fails, the job retries and regenerates the export; the leftover zip/document row is accepted. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

export.ts:214-283: the accountant notification after upload is wrapped in try/catch with a warning (best-effort). A crash before it leads to a BullMQ retry that regenerates the zip and re-sends. The `!pathTokens` path condition is infeasible but irrelevant. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

transactions/process-attachment.ts:47-99: in-place upsert of the HEIC->JPEG conversion, then the tax fields are updated. A retry (transactions queue attempts 3) re-converts (sharp accepts JPEG) and re-extracts, so it converges. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

transactions/process-attachment.ts:112-131: the process-document trigger is explicitly non-critical (try/catch, 'Don't fail the entire process'), after an idempotent in-place upload. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

bot/inbox-upload.ts:145-171: the file is uploaded to vault, then createInbox runs. If the insert fails, callers (bot/runtime.ts:748-783, rest/routers/chat.ts:101-120) only log a warning, with no retry or cleanup, leaving an orphan vault file with no inbox item. Unlike the worker jobs, nothing re-runs this. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

sync-account.ts:206,241-257: the uploads are upserts and the only missing step is an informational inbox_new notification. The trigger.dev retry (maxAttempts 3, line 32) reprocesses, and a lost notification is harmless. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

onboarding.ts:33-49: if the task stops after resend.contacts.create, the trigger.dev default retry (trigger.config.ts maxAttempts 3) re-runs. Re-creating the contact is harmless (the Resend SDK returns errors rather than throwing), and the welcome email is then sent. (Labeled 2026-11-06 by a separate AI agent: a new finding after the DEV-148 built-in SDK effects.)

If enqueueing the process-attachment job fails after the uploads succeed, the handler only logs and returns a 500 (index.ts:365). The vault file is then left with no inbox processing, and nothing in the code cleans it up or reconciles it. Any redelivery by the email provider would upload a new copy, because file names get a random nanoid suffix (utils.ts:52-57), so the first file stays orphaned.

The inbox_new notification is explicitly fire-and-forget: a comment calls it a non-critical side effect, and a .catch only logs the failure (utils.ts:163-185). Losing it after the uploads is an accepted, best-effort outcome.

The delete path removes each job separately after the transaction commits, so a failure can leave some delayed jobs in the queue. A comment documents this ordering (invoice-recurring.ts:557). The transaction has already reset the invoices to draft (:548), and ScheduleInvoiceProcessor skips any invoice whose status is no longer 'scheduled' (schedule-invoice.ts:35-41), so leftover jobs do nothing when they fire.

The pause path has the same pattern: invoices are reverted to draft inside the transaction (:618), then jobs are removed one by one with a comment explaining the order (:627-632). The worker's status check (schedule-invoice.ts:35-41) turns any job left behind into a no-op.

The delete on transactionAttachments only runs when status === 'deleted' (inbox.ts:1086-1100). On this path, updateInbox is only ever called with 'analyzing', 'pending' or 'suggested_match' (inbox-matching.ts:118-130, 161-165, 177-181, 211-215), and triggerMatchingNotification never calls it. The account update at process:58 commits before the transaction batches at process:93 (transactions.ts:2081). The window is real. The transactions queue retries jobs three times (transactions.config.ts:14), BaseProcessor.handle rethrows retryable failures (base.ts:245-246), and shouldProcess defaults to true (base.ts:319-321). Retrying overwrites the same account and transaction base values; there is no increment or completion guard skipping the failed batch. Classify as a retried recomputation job, not an impossible window or a guaranteed permanent inconsistency. Exhausted retries or non-retryable errors can still leave stale derived values.
